answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before its votes count, then cap the influence of accounts funded from the same recent source. A sybil operator must acquire and immobilize real capital for every identity, while splitting funds risks linking the accounts and triggering the cap. The sable, pearl, and ember agents may each vote, but multiplying names no longer multiplies cheap influence; the attacker pays an opportunity cost and risks losing the locked stake for provable rule violations.
